description:
## Intent

Graduate the Swift helper from a bare bundle-less binary to a **flat `.app` bundle inside the npm tarball**, because two wanted capabilities are impossible without a bundle: **UNUserNotificationCenter threshold alerts** and the **SMAppService login item** (plan, UI section: *"Notifications/SMAppService need the flat `.app` (v0.5 — or earlier if D4's notarization prototype forces it)"*). Then distribute via **brew**, where the cask depends on the D4/T-016 signing + notarization outcome — and NO-GO is an explicitly allowed outcome of that gate, so the cask deliverable here is conditional (ISS-044), not assumed.

Packaging precedent and constraint: **node-notifier** ships a `.app` in an npm package, and **npm tarballs cannot hold symlinked `.app` structures — flat only** (no `Contents/MacOS` symlink tricks; every entry a real file). This is why the plan calls it the *flat* `.app`.

Note the pull-forward clause: T-016's finding that notarization tickets do NOT staple to bare executables means D4 may already have forced an early flat `.app` in v0.3, or T-019's popover spike failure may have; if so, this ticket's bundle work is partially done and it becomes notifications + SMAppService + cask on top of the existing bundle.

## Scope

**In:**
- Flat `.app` bundle built in CI (universal, both slices, lipo), shipped in the main npm tarball; tarball-level release tests extended to bundle structure/modes/slices/signature (plan, UI/CI section).
- **UNUserNotificationCenter threshold alerts**: opt-in, permission-prompting only when the user enables them — never at install or first run (consistent with the plan's permissions phrasing: no permission prompts *expected* by default).
- **SMAppService login item**: replaces or augments the launcher-based LaunchAgent path for launch-at-login (T-020's toggle re-targets to it).
- **Brew distribution, conditional on the D4/T-016 outcome** (T-016: "Outcome feeds v0.5 brew-cask plans"): on GO, the notarized cask; on NO-GO, the recorded alternative (see approach notes) — never a criterion quietly ignored.

**Out:** quota mode, floating widget, own-the-parsing (T-022); the popover itself (T-019).

## Approach notes

- The no-quarantine/no-Gatekeeper evidence is **scoped to the npm extraction path, n=1, npm 10.9.3** (plan, Empirically verified). A brew cask download is a different path — quarantine behavior there is unproven and needs its own first-launch verification, on top of whatever T-016 established.
- **T-016 NO-GO path (ISS-044)**: NO-GO is an allowed outcome of the T-016 gate, so this ticket must be completable under it. On NO-GO, the notarized cask is off the table; the two admissible outcomes are (a) brew distribution is explicitly dropped for v0.5 with the decision recorded on this ticket, or (b) an npm-wrapping brew formula ships instead — installing through the npm extraction path whose no-quarantine evidence exists — validated end-to-end on a clean machine. Which of (a)/(b) is chosen is decided against T-016's actual findings and recorded before this ticket closes (open question 6).
- Tarball size: the bundle adds files; CI's packed-size measurement with the 1 MB threshold triggering the platform-split revisit still applies (a hard CI gate per ISS-035's resolution on T-014).
- SMAppService adoption must not break the T-015 upgrade matrix (upgrade/downgrade/prefix change/nvm removal/interrupted install) or the stop/start sequencing; any migration from LaunchAgent to SMAppService needs the matrix re-run.
- Threshold alerts consume snapshot data the service already computes (burn/blocks); the alert decision should live where the data lives, with the helper as the notification presenter.

## Constraints

- Zero lifecycle scripts still holds — the bundle must work from plain extraction, no postinstall assembly.
- `package.json` must never carry an author field or the maintainer's name; the same anonymity rule extends to bundle Info.plist metadata and cask/formula authorship as far as tooling allows.
- `usage.py` frozen; no real transcript data or personal paths in fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The npm tarball contains a flat .app bundle (zero symlinks anywhere in the tarball, verified by the tarball-level release test), and `npm pack` → clean-prefix install → helper launch works with lifecycle scripts disabled on npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun
2. Notifications are OFF by default; enabling them in settings triggers the UNUserNotificationCenter permission prompt at that moment (not at install/first-run), and a crossed spend threshold then produces a user-visible notification
3. Login item registration works via SMAppService from the bundled .app, and the T-020 launch-at-login toggle drives it; a package upgrade followed by the documented heal/repair path leaves login-item behavior working (upgrade-matrix re-run for the affected paths)
4. Conditional on the T-016 outcome (ISS-044): **on GO**, a brew cask installs the artifact chosen by the D4/T-016 outcome and first launch on a clean machine passes Gatekeeper on the cask path (online case at minimum; offline behavior recorded). **On NO-GO**, this criterion is satisfied by exactly one of: (a) a recorded decision on this ticket explicitly removing brew distribution from v0.5 scope, or (b) an npm-wrapping brew formula installed and verified end-to-end on a clean machine (install → helper launch → menubar renders). Closing the ticket with the cask requirement silently unmet is not an outcome
5. CI-measured packed tarball size is recorded; exceeding the 1 MB threshold fails the gate and the platform-split revisit is explicitly opened rather than silently ignored
6. Info.plist and cask/formula metadata carry no personal-name attribution

## Risks
The whole ticket sits downstream of T-016 — and with the Apple Developer membership already paid (owner decision, 2026-08-02: N-002), a NO-GO can only be technical (notarization/stapling failing for the artifact shapes tested), not a cost decision. A NO-GO kills the notarized cask; the conditional criterion 4 keeps this ticket satisfiable under that allowed outcome instead of impossible as previously written. The npm-path no-quarantine evidence does NOT transfer to the cask download path — an unverified Gatekeeper story there could ship a broken first launch. Migrating login-item mechanics to SMAppService risks regressing the hard-won T-015 upgrade matrix. Bundle growth may cross the 1 MB packed threshold and force the platform-split decision.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Did D4/T-016 (or a failed T-019 spike) already force the flat .app earlier? If so, re-scope this ticket to notifications + SMAppService + cask only.
2. Does SMAppService fully replace the launcher-targeted LaunchAgent for the menubar view, or only for launch-at-login while `service` keeps the LaunchAgent? The plan names both mechanisms without an integration ruling.
3. What exactly does the brew cask install — the .app alone (menubar-only users), or is cask a second full-product channel alongside npm? Plan says only "brew cask distribution".
4. Threshold-alert configuration: which thresholds (daily $? block burn rate?), where set, and defaults — plan is silent beyond "threshold alerts (opt-in)".
5. Signing identity (carried from N-002; the $99/yr cost question is RESOLVED — membership is paid, so T-016 is purely technical): a Developer ID certificate embeds the account holder's legal name, visible via `codesign -dv` — personal vs organization identity must be decided before signing anything shipped.
6. If T-016 returns NO-GO: which alternative discharges the brew deliverable — drop brew for v0.5 (4a) or ship the npm-wrapping formula (4b)? Decide against T-016's actual findings and record on this ticket.
title: Flat .app bundle: notifications + SMAppService; brew cask
